svg.title: Business-Name Claim Gates
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-business-name-gates; chapter number: 5; title: Business-Name Claim Gates; subtitle: Four checks before filing on a company balance; chart type: decision_tree; nodes: gate: G1; question: Was the company entered in the last-name field with the first name left blank?; pass next: G2; fail action: Re-run with the company in the last-name field and legal suffixes like LLC, Inc., or Corp. dropped on the first pass.; gate: G2; question: Have DBAs, prior names, acronyms, FEIN, and former office zip codes all been searched?; pass next: G3; fail action: Stack every name variant and old zip code; check federal sources separately because federal agencies are exempt from state escheatment.; gate: G3; question: For a merged or dissolved entity, is the full ownership chain documented?; pass next: G4; fail action: Pull certified articles of merger or dissolution plus a certificate of good standing; budget 6 to 12 months for the lineage audit.; gate: G4; question: Is the locator fee inside the state cap and past the unenforceable window?; pass next: File, then calendar the payout; South Carolina checks void at 90 days and force a full refile.; fail action: Hold; Missouri voids deals in the first 12 months, Colorado in the first 24 months with a 10% cap, and Georgia caps general agents at 10%.; caption: Most business-name misses come from searching wrong; these gates catch the common traps before a claim is filed.; assumptions note: Gate order reflects search-then-document-then-fee sequencing; state rules cited are as reported by the named channels and vary by state.; note: Attributed to Как се прави; GardenShop.Pro; Garden Shop Pro; Surplus Institute / David Church.

rect.title: gate: G1; question: Was the company entered in the last-name field with the first name left blank?; pass next: G2; fail action: Re-run with the company in the last-name field and legal suffixes like LLC, Inc., or Corp. dropped on the first pass.

gate: G2; question: Have DBAs, prior names, acronyms, FEIN, and former office zip codes all been searched?; pass next: G3; fail action: Stack every name variant and old zip code; check federal sources separately because federal agencies are exempt from state escheatment.

gate: G3; question: For a merged or dissolved entity, is the full ownership chain documented?; pass next: G4; fail action: Pull certified articles of merger or dissolution plus a certificate of good standing; budget 6 to 12 months for the lineage audit.

gate: G4; question: Is the locator fee inside the state cap and past the unenforceable window?; pass next: File, then calendar the payout; South Carolina checks void at 90 days and force a full refile.; fail action: Hold; Missouri voids deals in the first 12 months, Colorado in the first 24 months with a 10% cap, and Georgia caps general agents at 10%.

text.title: Assumptions: Gate order reflects search-then-document-then-fee sequencing; state rules cited are as reported by the named channels and vary by state.
text.tspan: Assumptions: Gate order reflects search-then-document-then-fee sequencing; state rules cited are as reported by the named channels
